ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that line $l_{1} \parallel l_{2} \parallel l_{3}$. Line AC intersects lines $l_{1}$, $l_{2}$, and $l_{3}$ at points A, B, and C, respectively. Line DF intersects lines $l_{1}$, $l_{2}$, and $l_{3}$ at points D, E, and F, respectively. Lines AC and DF intersect at point O. If BC = 2AO = 2OB and OD = 1, then what is the length of OF?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
Solution: $\because BC = 2AO = 2OB$,\\
$\therefore OC = 3AO$,\\
$\because$ line $l_1 \parallel l_2 \parallel l_3$,\\
$\therefore \frac{AO}{OC} = \frac{OD}{OF}$,\\
$\therefore \frac{AO}{OC} = \frac{OD}{OF} = \frac{1}{3}$,\\
$\because OD = 1$,\\
$\therefore OF = \boxed{3}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows three horizontal parallel lines labeled l1, l2, and l3. A downward-slanting transversal AC meets them at A on l1, B on l2, and C on l3. An upward-slanting transversal DF meets them at D on l1, E on l2, and F on l3. The two transversals intersect at O, which lies between l1 and l2. Reasoning: Given BC = 2AO = 2OB, we get 2AO = 2OB, so AO = OB, and also BC = 2AO. Since O, B, C are collinear in that order on AC, OC = OB + BC = AO + 2AO = 3AO. Thus AO/OC = 1/3. Because l1 is parallel to l3, triangles OAD and OCF are similar, so AO/OC = OD/OF. Therefore OD/OF = 1/3. With OD = 1, we have 1/OF = 1/3, hence OF = 3.
